clinician.trajectory_summary: A woman in her 60s with a history of bilateral mastectomy for breast cancer presented 3 weeks after elective surgical repair of idiopathic scoliosis with escalating midline abdominal pain and a palpable lump. Initial CT showed a small hematoma. Repeat CT performed weeks later due to increased pain and failure of analgesic therapy revealed a 3.2×1.5 cm hyperdense subcutaneous lesion in the upper midline abdominal wall that had increased in size compared to initial imaging. Ultrasound confirmed a 2.9×2.1×1.5 cm irregular lobulated hypoechoic mass in the left paramedian abdominal wall with internal vascularity, and biopsy was recommended. She underwent surgical resection of the mass with abdominal wall repair and mesh placement. Final pathology was consistent with desmoid fibromatosis with negative surgical margins. Postoperatively, her pain resolved completely and she recovered uneventfully.
